keyAndScale.modalCharacter: E Mixolydian driven by flattened 7th (D5) power chords and high-velocity Aussie pub-rock swagger

scalesUsed.name: E Minor Pentatonic
scalesUsed.application: Drives Rick Brewster's razor-sharp, staccato intro riffs and aggressive lead solo fills

scalesUsed.name: E Mixolydian
scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: Forms the harmonic framework for the verse and chorus movement between E5, D5, and A5

scalesUsed.name: E Blues Scale
scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - A# - B - D
scalesUsed.application: Injected across the guitar solo for raw, snarling attitude and chromatic passing bites

mainProgression.description: High-octane Australian pub-rock riff built on stabbing downstrokes, tight palm muting, and climbing power chords

sectionProgressions.description: The quintessential Brewster brothers twin-guitar punch with open low E chugging and syncopated stabs
Relentless eighth-note pedal chug building kinetic energy underneath Doc Neeson's theatrical vocals
Anthemic classic rock cadence delivering the unforgettable hook with full-throttle power

harmonicFunction: E5 (Tonic I): Relentless tonal anchor driven by machine-gun low E downstrokes
D5 (Subtonic ♭VII): Injects iconic Mixolydian drive, eliminating leading-tone resolution for hard-rock grit
A5 (Subdominant IV): Creates classic blues-rock lift resolving with authority back to the tonic E
G5 (Mediant ♭III): Provides bluesy chromatic tension in the main riff and intro hook

techniques.name: Rapid Downstroke Palm Muting
techniques.description: High-speed 154 BPM downstroke chugging on the open low E string requiring stamina and wrist relaxation

notes: Anchor the fleshy heel of the picking hand lightly across the bridge saddles
Keep pick strokes compact and strictly parallel to the strings for punchy percussive attack
Release the mute abruptly when striking accented power chord stabs

techniques.name: Twin-Guitar Harmonic Synchronization
techniques.description: Interlocking rhythm and lead guitars engineered to create a massive wall of sound without muddiness

notes: One guitar focuses strictly on low-register rhythm chug while the other adds biting upper-string stabs
Match vibrato rate and pick attack timing precisely between players
Use complementary amp EQ settings (one mid-forward, one low-mid heavy)

sections.name: Iconic Twin-Guitar Intro Riff
sections.description: One of the most famous guitar openings in Australian music history, featuring razor-sharp E5 stabs and climbing G5-A5 accents
notes: Attack the open E power chords with aggressive, short downstrokes
Slide crisply from G5 on the 3rd fret to A5 on the 5th fret
Leave complete silence during the staccato rests to create dramatic tension

sections.name: Driving Verse Chug & Stabs
sections.description: Fast-paced eighth-note pedal chugging building continuous momentum under the theatrical verse storytelling
notes: Maintain an unwavering palm-muted low E eighth-note pulse at 154 BPM
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 with sharp, unmuted power chord stabs
Lock closely with the bass drum for maximum pub-rock punch

sections.name: Anthemic Pub Rock Chorus
sections.description: The explosive chorus hook ('Take a long line, reel him in...') letting open power chords ring out
notes: Let the opening E5 power chord roar with full sustain
Execute rapid changes to D5 and A5 on the upbeat
Drive the turnaround hard into the next measure

sections.name: Rick Brewster Fiery Lead Solo
sections.description: Rick Brewster's blistering guitar solo, delivering sharp whole-step bends and ferocious staccato phrasing
notes: Position your hand at the 12th fret box for maximum bend leverage
Execute the 15th fret high E bend with reinforcement from index and middle fingers
Apply Rick Brewster's trademark laser-focused, tightly controlled vibrato

guitar.recommended: Gibson SG Standard or Fender Stratocaster with bridge humbucker
alternatives: Gibson Flying V (used by John Brewster)
Fender Telecaster with hot bridge pickup
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for razor-sharp Australian pub-rock mid bite and attack

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W or 100W Super Lead Head through 4x12 Celestion Greenbacks

effects.distortion: Natural British tube saturation pushed with an MXR Micro Amp clean boost
effects.reverb: Dry studio recording with minimal room reflections for in-your-face punch
effects.other: Albert Studios analog console compression (George Young / Harry Vanda production)

beginner.title: Power Chords & Rhythmic Stabs
steps: Learn the E5, G5, A5, and D5 two-finger power chord shapes
Practice the staccato stops with metronome at 110 BPM
Focus on eliminating extraneous string noise

intermediate.title: Speed & Endurance
steps: Build stamina for continuous 154 BPM downstroke palm muting
Seamlessly transition between verse chug and chorus open chords
Play along with the studio track from start to finish without pausing

advanced.title: Solo Precision & Live Swagger
steps: Master Rick Brewster's 15th and 17th fret bends with pinpoint pitch accuracy
Develop high-speed alternate picking on pentatonic string transfers
Capture the aggressive, theatrical Albert Productions dynamic feel

commonMistakes: Tensing the right forearm during the 154 BPM downstroke chug
Failing to mute the open strings during the dramatic staccato stops
Under-bending the 15th fret notes in the lead solo
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Right-hand downstroke endurance warm-up at 120 BPM
10 mins: Slow metronome drill on the G5-A5 slide and staccato rests at 135 BPM
10 mins: High-position pentatonic bending and vibrato practice
5 mins: Full song playthrough at full 154 BPM performance speed
focusAreas: Right-wrist relaxation and consistent pick depth
Tight, abrupt muting between power chord hits
Intonation and pitch control on whole-step bends
metronomeWork: Start at 120 BPM establishing steady downstroke stamina
Work up to 138 BPM focusing on clean chord transitions
Lock into 154 BPM matching the frenetic live energy of The Angels
